open_points.subject: Contract activation after trial-corpus growth
open_points.text: “an activation binds a contract version to one admitted implementation” / “activation ... requires an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus” / “the current activation of a contract version is the one recorded last”
open_points.question: When a trial case is added and the current implementation has no admitted verdict over the enlarged corpus, does its existing activation remain usable, become inactive, or trigger automatic readmission?
options: Keep the existing activation usable until another activation replaces it
Invalidate the existing activation until that implementation is admitted over the enlarged corpus
Automatically readmit the current implementation and retain or remove its activation according to the result
open_points.default_guess: Keep the existing activation usable, because no deactivation lifecycle or automatic readmission action is defined.

open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict” / “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions”
open_points.question: If the same implementation is submitted again against the unchanged corpus, is the existing verdict and evidence reused, or is a new admission observation created with new TrialExecutions and decided_at?
options: Reuse the existing AdmissionVerdict and its TrialExecutions
Create a new AdmissionVerdict entity for every admission run
Rerun the trials but replace or mutate the existing verdict
open_points.default_guess: Create a new admission entity for each run, because its TrialExecutions and decision time are new observations.

open_points.subject: ProofResult
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result” / “whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes)”
open_points.question: How is ProofResult identified when the same immutable flow version can produce an unproven result before binding acceptance and a proven result afterward?
options: Treat each result as an ephemeral value whose full result facts determine equality
Identify a result by the flow version plus the proof-time dependency state
Persist separate proof observations as entities
Require one invariant result per flow version
open_points.default_guess: Treat ProofResult as an ephemeral computed value that may differ when its external proof dependencies change.

open_points.subject: Flow mapping and port cardinality
open_points.text: “`cardinality`: `one` or `many` — `many` is what a map runs over” / “`map_over`: the one input port a `many` edge maps the node over, when mapped” / “each output collects one result per element”
open_points.question: Which endpoint makes an edge `many`, what source and destination cardinalities are valid for mapped and ordinary edges, what value does the mapped invocation receive, and what cardinality do its collected outputs have?
options: A mapped input port is declared `many`; each invocation receives one item and every output is lifted to `many`
A `many` source maps into a `one` input; each invocation receives one item and outputs are collected as `many`
A `many` input normally receives the whole list unless `map_over` explicitly changes it to per-item invocation
open_points.default_guess: Treat an ordinary `many` input as one list-valued invocation and `map_over` as explicit per-item invocation whose outputs are collected as `many`.

open_points.subject: Installation credentials and Actor identity
open_points.text: “names are unique in an installation, and a configuration repeating one is refused at start” / “`owner_token`, `agent_tokens`: each agent token with its name and whether it may author”
open_points.question: Must token values also be unique, including between the owner token and agent tokens, and what actor is authenticated if two configured principals share one token value?
options: Refuse any duplicate token value across the owner and all agents
Require uniqueness only among agent token values
Allow duplicate token values and define a precedence rule
open_points.default_guess: Refuse any duplicate token value across all configured principals so one credential always identifies exactly one Actor.
